articles.title: Closures, IIFEs, and private fields do not hide your JavaScript
articles.excerpt: A well-meaning review comment still shows up on pull requests: "wrap it in an IIFE so nobody can call it from the console." Sometimes the suggestion is a closure, a revealing module, or a #private fie…
articles.body: A well-meaning review comment still shows up on pull requests: "wrap it in an IIFE so nobody can call it from the console." Sometimes the suggestion is a closure, a revealing module, or a #private field. The intent is reasonable. The protection is not real. Anything that runs in the browser is reachable. Scope is a language rule for your program, not a boundary against a reader who already has the source. This article is about what closures and private fields actually do, how an attacker walks around them, and what to protect instead. Scope is not a security boundary JavaScript scope decides which names a function can see. It is invaluable for encapsulation. It does not stop someone from reading, rewriting, or hooking the same function.
articles.author: VEILVM

articles.title: We Wanted AI Agents. We Built an Org Chart.
articles.excerpt: We spent years complaining about meetings, handoffs, and layers of management. Now we’re building AI agents that do all three. A small coding task arrives, and somehow it needs a product manager, an a…
articles.body: We spent years complaining about meetings, handoffs, and layers of management. Now we’re building AI agents that do all three. A small coding task arrives, and somehow it needs a product manager, an architect, a reviewer, and someone to coordinate the other agents. The button is still broken. The org chart looks fantastic. Imagine asking an AI to fix a button that saves a form twice. You want it to save once. This feels like a reasonable assignment. Before the code changes, though, a product agent turns the request into requirements. An architect agent proposes a solution. A lead agent breaks it into tasks. A developer agent gets assigned the work. A reviewer agent waits for the output. Above them sits an orchestrator, making sure the other agents are sufficiently coordinated.

articles.title: A screenshot can't show a site that moves, so I rebuilt my portfolio around videos
articles.excerpt: For a long time my portfolio was a grid of screenshots. The problem: most of the sites I build move. A loader, a scroll-driven hero, a checkout flow. A screenshot shows none of that. So I rebuilt it w…
articles.body: For a long time my portfolio was a grid of screenshots. The problem: most of the sites I build move . A loader, a scroll-driven hero, a checkout flow. A screenshot shows none of that. So I rebuilt it with one rule: every project is told part by part, and every part has a video of the real site working. What's in it A home page with an introduction and a wheel of projects you move through by scrolling. A projects page grouped by type: e-commerce, landing pages and portfolios. A case study for each project: the problem, what was built, the decisions and the outcome, each part with its own video. An identity page with the logos and brand pieces I designed for clients. An about page with technologies, education and GitHub activity refreshed on every build.

articles.title: Claude Code with and without a stack-specific plugin on 4 real repos: what changed
articles.excerpt: I wanted a number instead of a feeling. Does giving Claude Code stack-specific skills, subagents and a guard hook actually change what it does on a real repository? So I wrote a plugin for each of fou…
articles.body: I wanted a number instead of a feeling. Does giving Claude Code stack-specific skills, subagents and a guard hook actually change what it does on a real repository? So I wrote a plugin for each of four stacks, and ran the same six prompts with and without it against a pinned commit of a real public repo. The setup Claude Code's plugin eval runner ( claude plugin eval ) runs each case in a scratch copy of the repo, once with the plugin and once without it ( --ablation with-without ), then scores the result with file checks and a judge model. Each case ran several times per arm (3 runs per case for Rails and Django, whose full output I kept), with Claude Sonnet.

articles.title: I built a website for my taxi driver friends in Buenos Aires: a scroll-driven flight, fixed fares and WhatsApp booking
articles.excerpt: Some friends of mine are taxi drivers. They've been driving in Buenos Aires for years, and recently they teamed up to offer fixed-price transfers from Ezeiza and Aeroparque airports and the cruise ter…
articles.body: Some friends of mine are taxi drivers. They've been driving in Buenos Aires for years, and recently they teamed up to offer fixed-price transfers from Ezeiza and Aeroparque airports and the cruise terminal. They had good cars and years on the street, but no site of their own: work came through referrals or through apps that take a cut. On the other side there's the traveler who lands at 6 a.m. with no idea what the ride will cost or whom to trust. That's who the site is for. What I built A cinematic hero: a drone flight over the Obelisco, synced to the scroll, frame by frame. Fixed fares in US dollars per route, with a quote tool that writes the WhatsApp booking message. A fleet showcase: six real cars with passenger and luggage capacity.

articles.title: Building a Commercial Construction AIoT Platform: Identify Sense Decide Act
articles.excerpt: For developers, the hard part of Construction AIoT isn't the model — it's the system around it. ‎ ‎Architecture thinking: ‎- Identify: Link zones, equipment, crews, materials, deliveries, and BIM elem…
articles.body: For developers, the hard part of Construction AIoT isn't the model — it's the system around it. ‎ ‎Architecture thinking: ‎- Identify: Link zones, equipment, crews, materials, deliveries, and BIM elements to operational history. Bad identity = bad alerts. ‎- Sense:Vibration, load, temperature, dust, noise, GPS, vision, drone imagery. Handle offline / intermittent connectivity as a first-class case — jobsites are not data centers. ‎- Decide: Prioritize safety risks, schedule drift, quality defects, and equipment health. Don't just alert — rank by impact and confidence. ‎- Act:Approved actions → alerts, workflow routing, access control, bounded equipment commands. Keep protection systems independent, define fallback behavior.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.body: On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster . The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.

articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase.

articles.title: Nvidia Reportedly Uninterested in Bringing Jensen Huang Back as CEO
articles.excerpt: Nvidia is reportedly not entertaining the idea of bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO following rumors that his allies had established a "war room" to push for his reinstatement.
articles.body: Nvidia is reportedly not entertaining the idea of bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO following rumors that his allies had established a "war room" to push for his reinstatement. The latest turn in the tech giant's whirlwind week arrived yesterday, when the Financial Times reported that the company's ex-boss had supported efforts from his friends in Silicon Valley to see him brought back into the fold . One source said these allies had assembled a "war room" to lay the foundation for his return, but it now seems those efforts may have been for naught. The Nvidia board of directors is not considering reinstating Huang as CEO after he resigned from his position Thursday, November 12, one source told CNBC .

articles.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX’s Starship, already the largest rocket on Earth, will get even bigger with next-gen V4 model
articles.excerpt: Just a day after SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket back at the launch pad for the first time ever, Elon Musk told us that the spacecraft will get even bigger.
articles.body: As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big. The company recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower. It was a huge moment for SpaceX , bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship. "Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15).
